Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National NRSA boss rejects calls to lobby Customs over right-hand drive vehicle restrictions Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 11:27am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Director-General of the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA), Abraham Amaliba, says he has rejected several requests to intervene with Customs to ease restrictions on the importation of right-hand drive vehicles into Ghana.
He said the requests followed discussions among stakeholders on a report examining the safety risks associated with such vehicles, particularly Toyota Voxy models, and indications that Customs would begin enforcing the restrictions.
Speaking on Joy FM's Super Morning Show, Mr Amaliba said Customs officials were not represented at the stakeholder meeting, but participants indicated that enforcement of the restrictions would commence.
The discussions followed a JoyNews special report titled “VOXY!! Blame Game Among State Institutions As Blood Flows On Ghana's Roads”, which highlighted frequent road crashes involving Toyota Voxy vehicles and raised concerns about their suitability for Ghana's road conditions.
Mr Amaliba said he subsequently received calls from individuals asking him to persuade Customs to relax the restrictions.
He, however, maintained that he would not intervene to support such requests.
“I received a number of calls asking me to talk to Customs to relax the ban, and I said I wasn't going to do that,” he said.
His comments come amid differing positions on the enforcement of restrictions on right-hand drive vehicle imports, with Customs reportedly denying that it is enforcing a ban.
Mr Amaliba also referred to correspondence from the Ministry of Transport in which the sector minister was reportedly asked to intervene with Customs over the matter.
